The Lorentz construction is dimensionally underspecified: it maps both z_i and Euclidean code c_j via exp_o but does not define tangent dimension, coordinate convention, or the relation between Euclid

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set λ=0 (or q_ij=0), retaining the same Poincare RQ-VAE, training schedule, seeds, and Stage3 setup; this tests whether behavior edges contribute.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-only q_ij and the Poincare distance in J_i(k), train SIDs, freeze them, then evaluate Stage3 Recall@10; compare with behavior-off and geometry-off runs and the frozen 0.063354 baseline.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep the identical training-only graph, q_ij, λ, and optimization, but replace every d_κ(x,y)^2 in the coupled objective with squared Euclidean distance; this tests whether curvature contributes beyond behavior regularization.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training interactions only, sort each user's training events by timestamp (or the dataset's documented sequence order), count adjacent directed pairs C_ij, compute destination counts n_j, retain top M outgoing neighbors under log(1+C_ij)/log(2+n_j), and row-normalize to q_ij. Do not construct edges across users or infer edges from validation/test sequences.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-next-item transition counts, discounted by destination popularity.
ideas.cost_estimate: Store at most M sparse outgoing edges per training item. The extra term is O(E_M) per assignment refresh and O(BM) per minibatch update, where E_M ≤ 24556M; it adds one hyperbolic center-to-center distance per retained edge and does not require all item pairs or a dense Sinkhorn matrix. At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs), there are 1,768,032,000 item-step opportunities, with edge work proportional to M times the items processed; assignment-refresh cost is paid 3000 times. For M=8, refreshes evaluate at most 196,448 edge terms each (589,344,000 across 3000 refreshes), plus minibatch edge terms; benchmark wall time against baseline because GPU batching and refresh implementation dominate.
ideas.coupling_equation: J_i(k)=d_κ(z_i,c_k)^2 + λ Σ_{j∈N_train(i)} q_ij d_κ(c_k,c_{a_j})^2; a_i=argmin_k J_i(k), where q_ij is the popularity-adjusted behavior weight and d_κ is the curved Poincare distance.
ideas.coupling_path: Training-only directed edges select successor assignments a_j; each item's candidate first-level codeword is then penalized according to the Poincare geodesic distances from that candidate codeword to those successor codewords. Removing the graph removes the neighbor-weighted term; replacing Poincare distance with Euclidean distance changes the actual grouping objective.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If items with shared directed successors are useful next-item alternatives, this cost will make first-level prefixes more predictive of successors and increase Stage3 test Recall@10, ideally beyond 0.065; observe changed first-token assignments and held-out Stage3 Recall@10, not SID quality alone. Keep only if the both-on run improves Recall over the frozen 0.063354 baseline and the specified ablations show both factors matter.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: First-level discrete assignment objective and its encoder/codebook gradients during RQ-VAE training; it acts on codeword-to-codeword transition-neighborhood cost, not merely item reconstruction distance.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Squared Poincare geodesic distance d_κ(x,y)^2 on the ball of radius 1/√κ, with fixed κ>0 (initialize κ=1; report it explicitly).
ideas.key_change: Precompute sparse, popularity-adjusted directed transition neighbors from training interactions, then add their expected hyperbolic codeword separation to each item's first-level assignment cost; alternate assignments and codebook updates with the usual RQ-VAE optimization. This changes which items share the first SID token, rather than only how an unchanged assignment measures reconstruction.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The graph, popularity counts, neighbor list, code assignments, and codebooks are constructed using the training split only. Freeze the resulting item-SID map before Stage 3 validation/test evaluation; no validation or test interactions, metrics, or derived transitions enter graph construction, refreshes, or training.
ideas.motivation: Ordinary itemwise reconstruction can spend first-level codewords separating visually or textually distinct items even when those items are interchangeable as next-item contexts; Stage 2 does not rank candidates, so prefixes should group items whose training-only successor neighborhoods overlap.
ideas.novelty: This makes directed transition-neighborhood similarity directly alter the first-level discrete assignment through a hyperbolic pairwise codeword cost. It is not a behavior suffix on fixed assignments, a shell-calibrated item-to-code distance, a Busemann gate, or a tangent-space warp.
ideas.observables: First-token assignment changes concentrated among items with overlapping training successor neighborhoods; training gradient/codebook updates include the sparse edge term; measure next-item predictability from SID prefixes and Stage3 validation/test Recall@10 under the existing evaluation protocol. The target is test Recall@10 > 0.065.

rebuttal.change: Revise the evaluation specification to require, alongside both-on and the existing geometry-off and behavior-off runs, a matched train-profile-shuffle control: permute complete nonzero directed profiles across item IDs before training, retaining their values, model, initialization, seeds, and budget. Report the actual transition counts/profile coverage and learned displacement norms, and compare SID changes and the existing Stage3 test_R@10 across both-on, shuffled-profile, and zero-profile runs; treat improvement over both controls plus profile-dependent SID changes as the evidence criterion. The zero-profile (or zero-warp) limit alone is explicitly not evidence for either contribution; the nonzero matched comparisons measure whether item-to-profile alignment contributes beyond generic warp capacity, and the geometry-off comparison tests the curved composition. This directly tests the hypothesized coupling without changing its mechanism or adding scores.
rebuttal.remaining: A positive controlled result would support this mechanism only on the specified dataset and evaluation; it cannot rule out all popularity or sparse-noise explanations, nor guarantee transfer to other settings.
rebuttal.unchanged: Training-only adjacent directed transition profiles, the learned bounded tangent displacement, Poincare exp-map/Mobius-add/log-map composition before the unchanged Euclidean RQ quantizer, ordinary reconstruction/VQ training, leakage boundary, and existing Stage3 Recall@10 outcome.

risks: Popularity correction may over-amplify noisy rare edges; the previous-assignment target can reinforce early mistakes or collapse neighboring items into a few codes; λ may overwhelm reconstruction; transition regularization may optimize training graph structure that does not transfer to test-time next-item behavior. The sparse edge term may add substantial runtime if assignment refreshes are not batched.
ideas.safeguards: Project all ball points to norm ≤(1-δ)/√κ (δ=1e-5); compute arcosh/log arguments with clamp ≥1+ε; use fp32 for distance and edge-weight accumulation; clamp denominators with ε=1e-8; normalize q over retained positive edges only; cap M and λ, clip gradients, and log the edge-term/reconstruction-term ratio and code usage to detect collapse. Resolve assignment ties deterministically. For items without outgoing training transitions, exactly recover the baseline first-level objective.
ideas.spec_equations: For each training user sequence, count adjacent transitions C_ij; define s_ij=log(1+C_ij)/log(2+n_j), N(i)=topM_j(s_ij), q_ij=s_ij/(Σ_{l∈N(i)}s_il+ε). At each epoch, with assignments a_j fixed from the prior refresh, compute J_i(k)=d_κ(z_i,c_k)^2+λΣ_{j∈N(i)}q_ij d_κ(c_k,c_{a_j})^2; choose argmin_k, update encoder/codebook via straight-through gradients on selected assignments and J_i(a_i), refresh assignments synchronously, then proceed to subsequent residual codebooks as in baseline. Use mini-batched edge lists; no dense N×N tensor.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only timestamp/order sequences, item IDs, encoder vectors z_i, first-level Poincare codebook {c_k}, κ, λ, and M. Output: first-level assignment a_i for every training item, updated encoder/codebook parameters, and ultimately frozen RQ-VAE SIDs for all catalog items. For catalog items absent from training edges, use N(i)=∅ and the standard reconstruction assignment.

specification.text: Let the training-only directed count be C_ij and item popularity n_j. Keep each i's top M successors by a_ij = log(1+C_ij)/(log(2+n_j)); normalize a_ij over its retained successors to q_ij. With first-level encoder point z_i and codebook points c_k in the Poincare ball of curvature -κ, assign a_i = argmin_k [d_κ(z_i,c_k)^2 + λ Σ_{j in N(i)} q_ij d_κ(c_k,c_{a_j})^2], using the previous-iteration assignments a_j for neighbor targets. Update encoder/codebook using straight-through hard assignments and the same summed objective (stop-gradient through a_j within the minibatch/epoch); rebuild assignments synchronously once per epoch to avoid order dependence. Continue ordinary residual quantization at later levels.

ideas.title: Allocate first-level codewords by directed transition neighborhoods in hyperbolic space
ideas.unresolved_objection: A positive controlled result would support this mechanism only on the specified dataset and evaluation; it cannot rule out all popularity or sparse-noise explanations, nor guarantee transfer to other settings.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set p_i(j) to the same fixed prior distribution for every item (equivalently disable transition-derived q_i), retaining Lorentz prototype distances and identical training budget; this isolates the contribution of user behavior.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-only p_i, hyperbolic maps, Lorentz distance, joint assignment score, and the same RQ-VAE schedule; evaluate Stage 3 Recall@10 and compare all runs under the frozen protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep p_i and the identical coupling path, but replace exp/log/Lorentz geodesic distance with Euclidean q_i and ||q_i-c_k||²; this isolates curved geometry.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage 2 training split only, count adjacent item pairs in each user's temporally ordered training sequence, optionally weighting each pair by inverse square root of its predecessor frequency; retain the top 32 successors per source, add ε=1e-4 smoothing to retained edges, and row-normalize. Do not form edges across split boundaries.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-next-item transition distributions, representing each item's observed successor branches.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse transition rows once in O(E_train); cache the q_i vectors. Per training step at the frozen scale of 24,556 items and 24 steps/epoch, score the current minibatch against K first-level prototypes, adding O(B*K*d) Lorentz distance arithmetic (typically a small constant-factor overhead over the first-stage assignment), with no all-pairs item calculation; 72,000 optimizer steps total over 3,000 epochs. Expect roughly 10–30% Stage 2 wall-clock overhead depending on batch size and K, plus one-time sparse preprocessing.
ideas.coupling_equation: h_i = exp_o(Σ_j p_i(j) log_o(y_j)); a_i = argmin_k [||z_i-e_k||² + λ d_L(h_i,c_k)²], where p_i is the behavior term and d_L is the curved term; L = L_RQ + λ d_L(h_i,c_{a_i})².
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions define p_i and hence curved item coordinate h_i=exp_o(Σ_j p_i(j)log_o(y_j)); that coordinate is compared to each hyperbolic code prototype to change first-level assignment and update both prototypes and successor embeddings. Removing transitions makes h_i item-independent/uninformative; replacing Lorentz distance/maps with Euclidean ones removes the curved allocation geometry.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: For items whose outgoing training transitions split into coherent successor branches, the joint score will place items with similar next-item opportunities under shared early SID prefixes while keeping semantic reconstruction adequate. Keep only if behavior-and-geometry-on improves Stage 3 test Recall@10 over the frozen 0.063354 baseline and both ablations, with the target exceeding 0.065; inspect first-level prefix transition predictability as a diagnostic, not as the admission criterion.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In first-level RQ-VAE code assignment and its selected-code training loss, where successor-distribution embeddings and code prototypes are compared before the SID prefix is emitted.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz-model squared geodesic distance d_L²(u,v)=κ⁻¹ arcosh²(-κ⟨u,v⟩_L), with trainable curvature fixed at κ=1 (negative sectional curvature -1); exp_o and log_o are the Lorentz/hyperbolic maps at the origin.
ideas.key_change: Before RQ-VAE training, compute each training item’s sparse distribution over its most frequent training-only successor items. During the first residual-quantizer stage, combine ordinary item-to-code distance with a hyperbolic distance from the item's transition-distribution embedding to a trainable prototype for each first-level code; use the resulting joint score for hard code assignment and reconstruction gradients.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Build and freeze T and p_i strictly from training interactions before SID training. Validation/test events are not read by preprocessing, prototype fitting, checkpoint selection, or code assignment; validation/test is used only by the separate Stage 3 evaluation protocol.
ideas.motivation: The Stage 2 reconstruction objective can preserve item vectors without organizing items into groups that are useful as next-item candidates. Items reached from the same predecessor often belong to distinct user-interest branches; encoding these branches into early SID assignments may make the generative recommender's prefix tokens more predictive.
ideas.novelty: This changes the first-level grouping objective using predecessor-conditioned transition distributions and hyperbolic prototype geometry. It is not a shell-calibrated per-item Poincare assignment, Busemann gate, or tangent-space warp: behavior changes which examples attract a prototype, and curved geometry is inside that same assignment score.
ideas.observables: The first SID token assignments and their member-item successor distributions should change; prefix-conditioned next-item predictability should rise on held-out training interactions, and the decisive observable is Stage 3 test Recall@10 relative to 0.063354 and the ablations.
risks: Sparse or noisy outgoing histories may make q_i unreliable; popularity-dominated successors can collapse branches; the hyperbolic term can dominate reconstruction or Lorentz optimization can become unstable. Tune λ on training-only diagnostics or fixed predeclared values, never test Recall.
ideas.safeguards: Compute Lorentz products in float32 or higher; clamp -κ⟨u,v⟩_L to at least 1+1e-6 before arcosh; clamp tangent norms before exp/log; project points onto the hyperboloid after each update and clip their spatial norm/radius; use ε-smoothed sparse rows and a zero/prior fallback for items with no outgoing training edge; normalize loss terms and cap λ (e.g. start at 0.01); check finite loss/gradients and fall back to Euclidean-only assignment for invalid rows.
ideas.spec_equations: Given sparse T, p_ij=(T_ij+ε)/(Σ_{r∈Top32(i)}T_ir+32ε) for j in Top32(i). Compute v_i=Σ_j p_ij log_o(y_j), h_i=exp_o(v_i). For first quantizer output z_i and codes e_k,c_k, score s_ik=||z_i-e_k||²+λ d_L(h_i,c_k)²; choose a_i=argmin_k s_ik, use straight-through one-hot(a_i), and optimize baseline RQ-VAE loss + λ mean_i d_L(h_i,c_{a_i})². Update y,c by backprop; export ordinary quantizer indices as SID prefix.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are ordered training-only user item sequences, Stage 2 item embeddings z_i, first-level Euclidean code vectors e_k, trainable Lorentz successor vectors y_j and code prototypes c_k, and λ. Outputs are first-level discrete assignments a_i, gradients for RQ-VAE and hyperbolic parameters, and ultimately standard multi-level SIDs.

specification.text: Let X be the items and T_ij be counts of adjacent (i,j) events in training sequences only. Row-normalize with additive smoothing over observed outgoing neighbors to obtain p_i(j). Map each successor item j to a trainable Lorentz-hyperboloid point y_j and each first-level code k to prototype c_k, both on curvature -κ (κ=1 initially). For each item form q_i = normalize(Σ_j p_i(j) log_o(y_j)), map q_i to the hyperboloid by exp_o, and set s_ik = ||z_i-e_k||² + λ d_L(exp_o(q_i), c_k)². Assign a_i=argmin_k s_ik; train encoder, Euclidean code vectors, y_j and c_k with the usual RQ-VAE reconstruction/commitment terms plus λ times selected hyperbolic term, using straight-through assignments. Normalize Lorentz points after updates and keep them within a bounded radius. At inference/export only the resulting standard discrete RQ-VAE codes are used.

ideas.title: Allocate shared SID prefixes by hyperbolic transition-branch prototypes

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Replace every b_i by the uniform K-vector while retaining Lorentz distances, compatibility parameterization, Sinkhorn, model size and training schedule; alternatively fix A contribution to zero log-prior. This tests whether user-interest information changes assignments.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use training-only soft user-interest mixtures, learned interest-code compatibility, Lorentz distances and identical minibatch Sinkhorn normalization; export hard RQ digits and evaluate the unchanged Stage3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep b_i, A and Sinkhorn exactly unchanged but replace exp_o and Lorentz geodesic squared distance with matched-dimensional Euclidean squared distance; retain the same temperature, logits, losses and seeds.
ideas.behavior_computation: For each training user, average the frozen embeddings of that user's training interactions (deduplicate or cap repeats); fit K-means with K=16 on these history vectors using training users only. Assign each user to a soft distribution q_u by softmax of negative squared distance to the fitted centroids with temperature τ_u. For each item i, b_ik ∝ ε + Σ_{training events (u,i)} q_uk; normalize b_i to sum to one. No chronological adjacency is used.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item soft mixture over latent user-interest components, computed only from which items training-split users consumed.
ideas.cost_estimate: One train-history clustering pass O(U*d*Iters) and event-to-mixture accumulation O(E_train*K) once; per tokenizer step adds O(B*K*C + B*C*iterations) for interest-code compatibility and Sinkhorn, alongside existing hyperbolic distance work (B items, C codes at the active level). At 24,556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3,000 epochs, the added compatibility work is about 1,768,032,000* K*C multiply-adds if recomputed for every item; cache b_i and A, and minibatch-only cost is 72,000 Sinkhorn calls of O(B*C*iterations), likely 5–20% wall-clock depending on B,C. No Stage3 inference cost is required after hard SIDs are frozen.
ideas.coupling_equation: s_{ij}= -d_{-c}(exp_o(z_i^l),exp_o(c_j^l))^2/τ + γ log(ε + b_i^T A_l[:,j]); P_l=Sinkhorn(exp(s)); z_i^l^2_{Lorentz} and b_i^T A_l[:,j] jointly determine P_l and the code update.
ideas.coupling_path: Training user-interest mixtures b_i and learned compatibility A determine a per-item prior over code choices; its log prior is added to Lorentz distance logits, changing the balanced responsibilities, codebook gradients and hard prefix digits. Removing b_i or replacing Lorentz distance changes this same assignment computation.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The item-interest mixture contains stable multi-user context information that content reconstruction misses; both-on should alter early-level SID groupings by matching items with similar interest mixtures, improve next-item separability and produce Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. Keep only if it beats frozen baseline and both controls under the same validation selection and seeds.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside each RQ level's soft assignment logits and consequent Sinkhorn responsibilities during Stage2 training, before choosing the code digit and updating the residual.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz hyperboloid exponential map at the origin and geodesic distance d_{-c}(X,Y)=acosh(max(1,-c<X,Y>_L))/sqrt(c), fixed curvature -c with c=0.5.
ideas.key_change: From training-only user histories, infer a small fixed set of user-interest components and represent each item by its smoothed distribution over those components. At each RQ level, use that distribution to modulate the hyperbolic soft code assignment before a minibatch Sinkhorn normalization; the resulting responsibilities drive codebook updates and straight-through hard SID choices.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Build user histories, centroids, soft assignments, b_i and compatibility initialization exclusively from the training interaction split; freeze centroids and b_i before SID fitting. Validation/test interactions do not contribute to user clusters, code assignments, optimization, or SID export; unseen items use the smoothed uniform b_i.
ideas.motivation: An item's single content vector can erase the fact that distinct training users consume it from different interest contexts; a useful SID prefix should group items that serve similar mixtures of user interests, not merely items with similar embeddings.
ideas.novelty: This uses user-level interest mixtures as a per-item soft assignment prior and combines that prior multiplicatively with hyperbolic code likelihoods in a balanced entropic assignment. It does not move each latent by its transition neighbors, match prefix occupancy to continuation mass, or use a behavior-only suffix.
ideas.observables: Measure per-level responsibility and hard-digit shifts, change in codebook/encoder gradients, similarity between items sharing prefixes versus b_i similarity, train-only held-out transition predictability by prefix, and Stage3 test Recall@10; report the behavior-off, geometry-off and both-on runs.

rebuttal.change: Specify that each RQ level's residual and code vectors are d-dimensional column vectors in the same fixed orthonormal coordinates on T_o H^d ≅ R^d, and that the Lorentz space is R^{d+1} with signature (-,+,...,+), curvature -c (c=0.5), and origin o=(1/√c,0,…,0). For every residual r_i^l and Euclidean code vector e_lj^l, use the same curvature-c Lorentz exponential map X_i^l=exp_o(r_i^l)=(cosh(√c
rebuttal.remaining: The proposal still requires selecting/reporting the implementation's RQ latent dimension d and validating numerical stability and empirical benefit; the specification defines how any chosen d is used but does not establish that the method improves Recall@10.
rebuttal.unchanged: Training-only user-interest mixtures b_i, learned compatibility A_l, Lorentz-distance-plus-interest-prior soft assignment with minibatch Sinkhorn and hard SID digits, and the baseline Euclidean RQ reconstruction/residual quantization and training losses.
rebuttal.why: |r||)/√c, sinh(√c||r||) r/(√c||r||)) and C_lj^l=exp_o(e_lj^l), with the continuous value at zero; dimensions must match and the map's spatial coordinates retain the tangent coordinate convention. The ordinary RQ reconstruction/residual update remains Euclidean and uses r_i^l−e_l,a; the Lorentz distance is an additional assignment term evaluated between the mapped versions of precisely those same current residual and candidate code vectors (not a separately dimensioned embedding). The interest-mixture prior and Sinkhorn assignment are otherwise unchanged, and exported digits remain hard choices from the combined assignment score. | This defines the tangent/Lorentz dimensions and coordinate convention, and explicitly links the Euclidean RQ quantities to the Lorentz points by a specified exp map, so the assignment is dimensionally well-defined without changing the mechanism or adding scores.

risks: User clusters may reflect popularity or noisy short histories; smoothing may wash out niche interests; minibatch balancing may impose artificial uniform capacity; compatibility parameters can collapse to a dominant component; Stage3 users may not share the training interest mixture distribution.
ideas.safeguards: Use float32/64 for maps and Sinkhorn; project Lorentz points back to the hyperboloid after updates; clamp acosh arguments to at least 1+ε and tangent norms before exp maps; stabilize log(b_i^T A) with ε; smooth rare items with a uniform Dirichlet prior; cap γ and logits, subtract row maxima before exponentiating, clamp Sinkhorn kernel, and fall back to row-softmax if nonfinite. Keep deterministic clustering and tie-breaking, monitor assignment entropy, code usage and gradient norms; ensure all clustering inputs are train-only.
ideas.spec_equations: History h_u=mean_{i in train(u)} e_i; fit centroids μ_k on {h_u}; q_uk=softmax_k(-||h_u-μ_k||²/τ_u). b_ik=(ε+Σ_{(u,i) in train}q_uk)/(Kε+n_i), then normalize. For level l, X_i=exp_o^{-c}(r_i^l), C_j=exp_o^{-c}(c_lj), A_l[:,j]=softmax_k(a_lkj). s_ij=-d_{-c}(X_i,C_j)^2/τ+γ log(ε+b_i^T A_l[:,j]); P=Sinkhorn(exp(s/τ_s)) with uniform row and column marginals. Quantized residual is Σ_j P_ij c_lj for training gradient; forward SID digit is argmax_j s_ij, followed by the baseline residual update. Keep γ modest (e.g. 0.1), K=16, Sinkhorn iterations=5; use the baseline reconstruction/commitment objective and straight-through path.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training user-item events, frozen item embeddings, Stage2 encoder residuals and codebooks, c, τ, τ_s, γ, and K=16. Outputs: frozen per-item interest mixtures b_i, trainable compatibility matrices A_l, differentiable level-wise responsibilities, updated codebooks/encoder, and hard SID digits.

specification.text: Let q_u be the normalized counts of user's items in K-means clusters fit to training-user history vectors (history vector is the mean of frozen item embeddings); freeze those clusters. Define b_ik=normalized sum over training events (u,i) of q_uk, with Dirichlet smoothing. For latent z_i and code c_lj, compute p_ij ∝ exp(-d_{-c}(exp_o(z_i),exp_o(c_lj))²/τ + γ log(ε + Σ_k b_ik A_ljk)), where A_ljk is a learned soft compatibility from interest component k to code j, row-softmaxed. Sinkhorn-normalize p over the minibatch to uniform code capacity, use p for the soft quantization/commitment update, and retain argmin of the same combined log-score for exported digits. Initialize A near uniform and γ small; train with the baseline reconstruction and VQ losses.

ideas.title: Transport user-interest mixtures into hyperbolic prefix assignments
ideas.unresolved_objection: The proposal still requires selecting/reporting the implementation's RQ latent dimension d and validating numerical stability and empirical benefit; the specification defines how any chosen d is used but does not establish that the method improves Recall@10.

per_scorer_objection.scoring_1: The bundle provides no measured coverage or support for the specific successor-overlap hypothesis, and prior ledger mechanisms already use directed assignment/geometry, making the purported novelty and transfer particularly uncertain.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_2: No measured evidence establishes that directed successor-neighborhood overlap is a problem or predicts useful first-token groupings; the bundle labels the behavioral mechanism proposed, while PRIOR_WORK is NOT_CHECKED and the ledger includes several directed-assignment mechanisms with mixed results.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_3: The bundles establish the transition signal and computation as proposed, but provide no measured support/coverage statistic for successor-neighborhood overlap; popularity-discounted rare edges may reinforce noise, while the cited directed assignment/geometry experiments make incremental novelty uncertain.

per_scorer_rationale.scoring_1: behavior_evidence=2 because E1-E3 define the signal and leakage boundary but supply no measured transition statistic or coverage. geometry_necessity=4 because E5-E8 place Poincare distance inside the behavioral assignment term and specify a Euclidean control, though cancellation/necessity is not established. novelty=2 because E9 is NOT_CHECKED and E14/E16/E19 show nearby directed assignment/geometry work. downstream_mechanism=4 because the stated assignment change is first-token grouping and prefix successor predictability is diagnostic, but measured support is absent. falsifiability=3 because three factor conditions and a baseline threshold are named, but matched settings and a discriminating failure diagnostic are incomplete. implementability=3 because sparse costs and update schedule are given, but differentiable/numerical safeguards and total minibatch cost are not fully resolved. exploration_value=1 because directed assignment/geometry is close to measured ledger mechanisms. UNKNOWN on support and prior-art check; bounded resolution: audit transition coverage and inspect the cited mechanism implementations.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_2: behavior_evidence=2 because the signal is specified but no measured behavioral statistic or coverage is supplied (E1-E4). geometry_necessity=3: a genuine curved pairwise geodesic term is coupled to behavior in assignment (E5-E8), but the provided material does not establish advantage over a matched Euclidean cost or rule out cancellation. novelty=2: distinct-looking edge-weighted center cost, but directed assignment, codeword geometry and tangent variants already appear in the ledger (E14-E21), and prior-art search is unchecked (E9). downstream_mechanism=4: first-token assignments are directly changed, with prefix predictability and Stage3 Recall named, but no directional diagnostic is fully operationalized. falsifiability=3: both factors are required and three comparisons are implied; matched budgets/seeds and a clear failure criterion are not fully specified. implementability=3: equations and sparse cost are provided, but minibatch/epoch stop-gradient and refresh details leave optimization/gradient implementation risk. exploration_value=2: a small variation within the already measured directed assignment/codeword geometry family. Recall values in the ledger are measurements of other arms, not this proposal.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_3: Behavior=3 because the directed signal and construction are explicit and testable (E1-E2), but not measured. Geometry=3: the curved center-to-center pairwise cost is genuinely in the coupled assignment (E5-E7), yet no argument shows a benefit over the matched Euclidean control (E8). Novelty=3 because the computation differs from the named mechanisms, but prior work is NOT_CHECKED and the ledger already includes directed assignment/geometry families (E9-E10, E14-E21). Downstream=4 for an explicit first-token assignment-to-prefix predictability-to-Recall chain; diagnostic direction is specified in the proposal. Falsifiability=3 because both-on and behavior-/geometry-off comparisons and a keep criterion are requested, but exact matched-control settings and a discriminating diagnostic are not fully fixed. Implementability=3: pseudocode and sparse cost are given, but stable Poincare distance safeguards and edge-free item handling are unspecified. Exploration=4 because pairwise successor-code geometry is a distinct mechanism whose failure would test whether transition neighborhoods should constrain codeword layout.

per_scorer_scope_reason.scoring_1: Training-only directed transitions, Poincare distance, and a coupled first-level assignment cost are specified; it changes assignments, and proposes behavior-off, Euclidean, and both-on comparisons, with observable assignment and Stage3 effects.
